ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the intersection of the line $y=-x+m$ and $y=nx+4n\ (n\neq 0)$ has an abscissa of $-2$. What are the integer solutions of the inequality $-x+m>nx+4n>0$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the given condition, for $y=nx+4n\ (n\neq 0)$, then $x=-4$. Thus, the solution set for $nx+4n>0$ is $x>-4$.\\
Since the $x$-coordinate of the intersection point between $y=-x+m$ and $y=nx+4n\ (n\neq 0)$ is $-2$, by observing the graph, the solution set for $-x+m>nx+4n$ is $x<-2$.\\
Therefore, the solution set for $-x+m>nx+4n>0$ is $-4<x<-2$.\\
Since $x$ is an integer, thus $x=\boxed{-3}$.
